I'm settling in to think about this year's planning as the farmer would — 35 years of experience talking.

---

## My thinking (as the farmer)

I'm 66 now. Been working these 10 mu for most of my life, same land my family's had. Just me and the wife in the house these days — our boy works in the city and sends money sometimes but he's not coming back to farm. So the two of us do what we can, and for the heavy work I pay the custom machinery folks. Can't swing a sickle anymore, my back won't take it.

Like most people in this village, I do wheat then maize, wheat then maize. That's how it's always been. Some people switched to cotton out west, but I stuck with grain because the custom harvester comes through reliably and the wheat-maize rotation is what I know. Changing at my age? No need.

**My wheat** — already in the ground. Put it in around October 10th last year after the maize came off. I use the Jimai variety the co-op sells, nothing fancy. My neighbor Lao Wang uses the same and his wheat always looks good, so it works. Drilled with the custom planter, about 15 kg of seed per mu.

For the wheat fertilizer, I did my usual — about 1.5 bags of compound 15-15-15 per mu as base before planting, then I'll topdress urea at jointing in March, about 15 kg per mu. My son-in-law who went to the agricultural school told me once I could cut back some, and the extension guy said the same. But I've seen what happens when you skimp and then get a dry spring — the wheat goes yellow and yields drop hard. I'd rather put down a bit extra and sleep easy. At 66 I'm not experimenting with my one harvest.

Irrigation — I'll run the well 3 times probably. Winter water in December if it's been dry, then at jointing in March, then at heading around late April. The electricity for the pump isn't cheap but without it on this dry North China land you get nothing. If it's a wet spring I skip one.

Herbicide I spray once in spring — can't keep up with the weeds by hand anymore.

**My maize** — goes in mid-June right after the wheat combine comes through. Very tight, 3 or 4 days usually. I don't plow — I haven't plowed in years. The no-till planter goes right in and drops the seed. Saves time, saves money, and honestly at my age plowing isn't an option.

Hybrid seed, always. I buy the packets from the agro-shop, usually Zhengdan 958 or whatever the dealer says is good that year. Everyone uses hybrid, the old seed doesn't yield.

Fertilizer for maize — same idea as wheat. Base compound about 1.5 bags per mu when I plant, then topdress urea 20 kg per mu at the big trumpet stage in early August. Maize is hungrier than wheat in my experience, that's why I put more urea on it.

Summer rain is usually enough for maize, I might irrigate once in July if there's a dry spell. I watch what the neighbors do — if Lao Wang's running his pump I probably should too.

Herbicide after planting, and sometimes I spray once for corn borers if I see the damage.

**Yields** — I figure 450 kg/mu of wheat and 500 kg/mu of maize in a normal year. Last year was about that. Some years better, some worse.

**Money** — total input cost for the year across both crops, probably 8-9 thousand yuan. Most of that is fertilizer and the custom machine fees. The pension helps with household, so the farm money mostly goes back into the farm.
